A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XRPO research. All 19 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original math and code benchmark results, training-convergence measurements, component ablations, hyperparameter experiments, and reasoning case studies.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds model and baseline comparisons, latency measurements, and several controlled analyses of ICL and rollout allocation.

M1.justification: The three core components and Equations (1)-(6) remain unchanged. However, Algorithm 1 changes its corpus-update comment from adding only correct, non-ICL rollouts to adding correct rollouts. V3 does not establish whether ICL-generated successes become eligible or whether this is merely abbreviated documentation.

E1.justification: The math and code task domains remain. Appendices D-F add evaluations with truncated demonstrations, weaker or random retrieval, and test-time ICL, extending input conditions within existing tasks. Newly identifying the training-data sources does not establish that the underlying training data changed.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates GRPO and GSPO. V3 adds three-component DAPO and TreePO Sampling to corresponding Qwen comparisons, and CurES in Appendix G. Table 5 also newly compares component ablations against DAPO and TreePO Sampling; these are evaluated comparators, not merely additional citations.

E3.justification: V3 adds Llama-3.2-3B with distinct generation and decoding settings, comparisons at k=4, 8, 16, and 32, and a latency experiment using batch size 64 and 256 rollouts per prompt. Figure 3a switches from pass@4 to pass@1. These extend evaluation protocols beyond the largely retained Qwen settings.

E4.justification: V3 adds an isolated rollout-planner ablation, allocator hyperparameter sensitivity, length-bias and truncation analyses, train-versus-test ICL controls, retrieval-quality experiments, and allocation-distribution diagnostics. Earlier AS/ICL ablations remain, but the two worked GSPO/XRPO reasoning comparisons in v1 Appendix B are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run counts, random seeds, significance tests, or benchmark confidence intervals. V3 retains the existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting across hyperparameter settings and extends it to another sweep. Added length z-scores and percentiles describe response distributions rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive benchmark and analysis results, including Llama average pass@1 of 4.48 versus GRPO's 4.17 and measured training overhead of 4.7%. LCBv5 scores and case-study outcomes disappear. Most matched Qwen3 scores remain, but new Table 5 reports HMMT pass@1/cons@32 of 21.66/23.33, conflicting with 22.29/26.67 retained in Table 1.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a limited latency model and derivation of large-budget and worst-case overhead behavior, absent from v1. The optimizer's existing mathematics remains unchanged. The new derivation's ceiling-to-fraction equalities in Equations (7)-(8) are not generally valid.

C1.justification: The three-component contribution and headline accuracy and convergence claims remain substantially the same. V3 explicitly extends the introduction's superiority claim to DAPO and narrows the ICL novelty assertion from effectiveness within RL generally to effectiveness within RLVR training.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations of correctness-gated shaping, context limits favoring shorter solutions, and training/test difficulty mismatch making test-time ICL unhelpful. It newly discusses limits on model scale and task diversity and possible teacher-generated exemplars. V1's case-specific interpretations of reasoning errors are removed.

D1.justification: V3 newly documents DAPO-Math-17k and DeepCoder training sources and sampling counts, corpus initialization, precomputed retrieval lookups, standard evaluation without ICL, and component timings. It also provides additional model settings and announces public code and datasets through an access link absent from v1.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to adaptive allocation, replay, and agent/meta-RL approaches, including CurES, GVM-RAFT, Knapsack RL, TreePO, CEL, LaMer, and RePO. V3 more explicitly positions runtime rollout allocation against prompt selection and distinguishes single-turn RLVR seeding from replay and multi-turn adaptation.

P1.justification: V3 merges background and related work, moves motivation into the method section, substantially rewrites existing motivation and positioning paragraphs, and reorganizes the experimental narrative and appendices. The ICL-template material is retained in Appendix C, while the former case-study appendix is replaced by organized analytical sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, adds a framework schematic and allocation histogram, and splits and expands result tables. Existing convergence plots move from main-text Figure 2 to appendix Figure 5. The boxed reasoning examples disappear, and the ICL template is reformatted.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses important validation gaps through relevant adaptive-sampling competitors, an isolated planner ablation, controls for test-time ICL, and measured per-step overhead. Training-source and implementation disclosures also substantially improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed LCBv5 scores and illustrative cases, although conflicting HMMT entries in Tables 1 and 5 and mathematical errors in Appendix B limit confidence in some additions.
